pull.title: test: measure rpcwaittimeout floor with monotonic time
pull.body:
Previously, `interface_bitcoin_cli.py` measured the `-rpcwaittimeout` wait floor with `time.time()`. `bitcoin-cli` arms that deadline with `std::chrono::steady_clock`, so a CI wall-clock step backward can make the elapsed time look short and cause the assert to fail.

Fix this by using `time.monotonic()` instead and using `-rpcwaittimeout=1`. The log line also now says "at least" so it matches the floor assert.

h/t ViniciusCestarii for suggesting `time.monotonic()` here.

`start_time` is taken before spawning bitcoin-cli and bitcoin-cli uses monotonic time, so the flake can only come from wall clock adjustment. Wouldn't replacing `time.time()` with `time.monotonic()` fix this without the slack?

events.body:
Good catch, not sure how I missed this. I presume I was confused by the LHS and RHS both doing addition. Maybe it would be clearer to understand and to read the assertion error message, when the LHS was `monotonic()-start_time`, so that only the duration is printed. Steps to reproduce:

```
faketime --exclude-monotonic -f "+0 x0.5" ./bld-cmake/test/functional/interface_bitcoin_cli.py 
```

test: measure rpcwaittimeout floor with monotonic time

Require the `-rpcwait` command to wait at least the configured timeout
period before raising a process error. Measure the wait using
`time.monotonic()` so that wall-clock discrepancies do not cause
intermittent test failures.

Also, lower the timeout from 5 to 1 second.
